description: Wi-Fi presentation schema. Describes access points, switches, floorplans, buildings, materials, attenuation/coverage areas, and survey paths for wireless planning, prediction, and visualization. Unknown properties are permitted for extensibility; vendor-specific extensions SHOULD use an "x-" property name prefix.
title: oi_wifi

building.description: A building that groups floorplans together with vertical ordering and transformation capabilities

wall_materials.description: Named wall materials referenced by wall_segment.wall_type (matched by exact equality against material.name).

openintent_version.description: Version of the openintent-wifi model. Values SHOULD follow semantic versioning (major.minor.patch), e.g. "2.0.1"; the format is not enforced so that legacy values remain valid.

floorplan_name.description: Name of floorplan to which this access-point belongs.

building_name.description: Name of the building with which to look for floorplan_name

serial_number.description: Serial number of this access point.

mac_address.description: MAC Address of an access point in the format 01:23:45:67:89:0a: two lowercase hex characters per octet, colon separated. Case is deliberately strict so values from different vendors are directly comparable; senders must normalize to lower case.

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name for this access point.

model.description: The model number of this particular access point

sku.description: SKU part number for this specific access-point.

connected_switch.description: Information about the switch this access point is connected to

switch_name.description: Reference to the name of the switch this access point is connected to

port.description: The port on the switch that this access point is connected to

vlan.description: VLAN ID assigned to this access point connection

closet_name.description: Name or identifier of the closet where the connected switch is located

switch_id.description: Vendor identifier of the switch to which this access point is connected. Must match switch.vendor_id of the referenced switch.

ssids.description: SSIDs available on this access point. Each entry is either a plain string (SSID name only) or an ssid object that can bind the SSID to specific bands.

antennas.description: Array of antennas connected to this access-point.

ethernet_ports.description: Names/labels of the wired Ethernet ports available on this access point (for example "eth0", "Gb1").

orientation.description: If there are no antennas defined, or the antennas are integrated, the orientation for access-point should be used.

coordinates.description: Array of coordinate objects locating this access point. Each entry may express the same physical position in a different unit or system (for example one "pixels" entry, one "meters" entry, and one lat/long entry); consumers select the representation that fits their use case. Entries must describe the same point.

display_color.description: Hex color code for visualizing access points. Has no inherent intent, but for visualization purposes. Should start with "#" to indicate a hex color value. Example '#AC7400'

ssid.description: An SSID broadcast by an access point

bands.description: Bands on which this SSID is broadcast. Omit if all client-access radios broadcast it.

floorplan_name.description: Name of floorplan to which this switch belongs.

building_name.description: Name of the building with which to look for floorplan_name

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name for this switch.

model.description: The model number of this particular switch

sku.description: SKU part number for this specific switch.

ip_address.description: Management IP address of the switch (IPv4 or IPv6)

closet_name.description: Name or identifier of the closet (Intermediate Distribution Frame) room/closet where this switch is located

coordinates.description: Array of coordinate objects locating this switch. Each entry may express the same position in a different unit or system; entries must describe the same point.

display_color.description: Hex color code for visualizing the switch. Has no inherent intent, but for visualization purposes.

vendor_id.description: Vendor-assigned unique identifier of the switch. Referenced by accesspoint.connected_switch.switch_id.

rack_units.description: number of rack units (RU) required for the device.

name.description: Unique name of floorplan (must be unique in the openintent payload.)

map_uri.description: URI (absolute or relative) where to retrieve the map. Not all URIs will be resolvable by all systems.

building_name.description: Name of the building with which to look for floorplan_name

floor_id.description: String representation of the floor id (Example: Ground, 1st, 3, etc)

rotation.description: Rotation of the floorplan from native orientation, in degrees, positive values counter-clockwise about the lower-left origin. Negative values are permitted. When this floorplan is placed by a building_floor.transform, the transform is applied on top of this rotation.

dimensions.description: Dimensions of the floorplan. Each entry expresses the same extent in a different unit (for example pixels, meters, and feet); consumers select the entry that fits their use case.

attenuation_areas.description: List of areas on the floorplan

coverage_areas.description: List of coverage areas on the floorplan

holes_in_floor.description: List of areas on the floorplan

type.description: Type of network equipment closet (IDF=Intermediate Distribution Frame, MDF=Main Distribution Frame)

coordinates.description: Array of coordinate objects locating this closet. Each entry may express the same position in a different unit or system; entries must describe the same point.

id.description: Radio id, if one is known. Optional for vendors that do not number radios.

radio_function.description: Intended role of the radio. SENSING is reserved for dedicated IEEE 802.11bf sensing operation.

band.description: Frequency band this radio operates in.

channel.description: Primary 20 MHz channel number. On 6 GHz, where channel numbering conventions differ between implementations, senders should also provide frequency_mhz.

frequency_mhz.description: Center frequency of the primary 20 MHz channel in MHz (for example 2462 for channel 11). Useful on 6 GHz and for implementations that identify channels by frequency.

channel_assignment.description: This defines if the radio channel is manually assigned (human) or dynamically assigned by tooling.

secondary_channel.description: Secondary channel number using 802.11ac center-channel notation. For non-contiguous widths (80+80_MHz), identifies the center of the segment not containing the primary channel.

transmit_power.description: Conducted, per-chain transmit power in dBm.

transmit_eirp.description: Effective Isotropic Radiated Power in dBi: conducted transmit power plus antenna gain.

mimo_chains.description: Number of radio chains this radio is operating with

antenna.description: An antenna connected to an access point, either integrated or external via RF connectors.

name.description: Optional handle for referencing this antenna from radios or documentation.

leads.description: The number of leads an antenna has.

extension.description: RF extension cable between the antenna and the access point.

extention.description: Deprecated spelling of "extension", accepted for backward compatibility. New payloads should use "extension".

antenna_type.description: Indicates if the antenna is classified as an omnidirectional or a directional antenna.

antenna_extension.description: An RF extension cable connecting an antenna to an access point.

is_extended.description: Is the antenna extended with an RF extension cable?

unit_length.description: Unit for describing the length of the extension

length.description: Length of the extension in the unit_length

losses.description: Array of losses per frequency band.

rf_connector.description: Details about RF connectors that would be present on an antenna or access point.

connector_type.description: Connector form factor. "Type-N" is a deprecated spelling of "TYPE_N"; the legacy value will be removed in a future release.

gender.description: Describes the gender of the RF connector

frequency_bands.description: Frequency bands this connector is rated for.

channel_width.description: Represents channel width configurations as a string. Note: 160+160_MHz is a vendor-specific configuration; 802.11 standardizes only 80+80 MHz as a non-contiguous width.

coordinate_xyz.description: A coordinate that references cartesian coordinates using x,y,z

x.description: Coordinate in X dimension represented as a number

y.description: Coordinate in Y dimension represented as a number

z.description: Coordinate in Z dimension as height from floor represented as a number

coordinate_lat_long.description: A geospatial coordinate expressed as WGS84 latitude/longitude in decimal degrees, plus optional elevation. (ISO 6709 is a separate string-encoded notation; this object carries the numeric equivalent.)

elevation.description: Height in meters above sea level

coordinate.description: A location expressed in either or both of the x/y/z and lat/long coordinate systems. At least one system must be present.

frequency_band.description: A frequency band that an antenna or radio operates in.

orientation.description: Object that describes the orientation of a device or antenna using aircraft-style attitude angles: rotation (yaw), tilt (pitch), and roll.

rotation.description: Describes the rotation (yaw) of the device in degrees, where 0 points toward the top of the floorplan and positive values rotate counter-clockwise, consistent with floor_transform.rotation. For omnidirectional APs, if looking at the AP on the ceiling, the direction points toward the top of the vendor logo. For directional antennas/APs, the peak beamwidth should point in this direction.

tilt.description: Describes the tilt (pitch) of the device in degrees. For integrated antenna APs or omnidirectional antennas, 0 describes the default orientation. For directional APs, 0 describes the antenna as pointed horizontal, with positive values tilting up, and negative values pointing down.

roll.description: Describes the rotation of the device about its own pointing axis. 0 describes the device's default orientation. This will normally be zero in most scenarios. Would be used to rotate an antenna from vertical to horizontal polarization.

dimension.description: Dimension of a floorplan where the origin is located in the lower left corner, making all references to location positive values

length.description: y (north-south) extent of the floorplan. Note the naming: length is the y dimension, width is the x dimension.

unit.description: The dimension unit for length, width, height.

wall_segment.description: Represents a line segment of a wall on a floorplan. Each segment requires a start, and end and a description for the wall type.

wall_type.description: Name of the wall type. If it exactly matches the name of an entry in wall_materials, that material's properties apply. Matching is by convention only and cannot be enforced by the schema. Prefer referencing a material over repeating attenuation values on every segment. If both a matching material and inline fields are present, this segment's inline fields override the material.

display_color.description: Used if wall_type does not match a named wall_material. Hex color code for visualizing this wall segment. Has no inherent intent, only for visualization purposes. Should start with "#" to indicate a hex color value. Example '#AC7400'

thickness.description: Used if wall_material is not defined. Thickness in meters of the wall.

height.description: Used if wall_material is not defined. Height of the top of the wall from the floor.

bottom_height.description: Used if wall_material is not defined. If wall does not start at floor, define at what height from floor

wall_point.description: Two-dimensional coordinate of a wall point, expressed in the floorplan's map units (see floorplan.dimensions).

reference_marker.description: A reference marker to denote a location on the floorplan. Can be used to provide notes, or a translation between coordinate systems.

name.description: Name of the reference marker, unique within its containing object (floorplan or access point).

material.description: Object that defines the properties of a wall or area material. Referenced by name from wall_segment.wall_type (wall_materials) and attenuation_area.area_material (area_materials).

name.description: Name of the material, unique within the wall_materials or area_materials array.

itu_material_type.description: ITU-R P.2040 material designation, if known

thickness_m.description: Thickness of the wall in meters. Do not fake wall thickness with arbitrary formulas. If wall thickness is not defined, omit and use flat attenuation values.

bottom_height.description: For walls, if the wall does not start at the floor, this allows you to specify the height the bottom of the wall is at.

top_height.description: For walls, the top_height is the height in meters of the top of the wall.

display_color.description: Hex color code for visualizing objects built from this material. Has no inherent intent, only for visualization purposes. Should start with "#" to indicate a hex color value. Example '#AC7400'

rf_properties.description: RF attenuation properties of a material. Values are positive numbers of dB lost (subtracted from the signal) on a path through the material.

attenuation_flat.description: Flat attenuation value in dB. The object attenuates by this value regardless of thickness.

attenuation_per_m.description: Attenuation in dB per meter of thickness. Multiply by material thickness to calculate total attenuation.

band_attenuations.description: Optional per-band overrides, since real materials attenuate differently across 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz. When an entry covers a band, it takes precedence over the band-independent values above.

attenuation_flat.description: Flat attenuation in dB for this band.

attenuation_per_m.description: Attenuation in dB per meter for this band.

area.description: An area is defined as a closed polygon with a list of coordinates. Coordinates must be listed in consecutive order around the perimeter, and the last coordinate must coincide with (repeat) the first coordinate to close the ring. Ring closure cannot be enforced by the schema; implementers should treat an unclosed ring as invalid.

attenuation_area.description: An area of a floorplan whose RF attenuation is defined by a material.

exclusion.description: When true, this area is excluded from the coverage requirement rather than targeted by it.

inverted.description: Inverted hole-in-floor objects describe a hole that is everywhere except the defined area. Example: to mark the exterior of a building as a hole, use an inverted area covering the building footprint.

path_point.description: A point to be used along a path with reference to the data structure.

timestamp.description: Timestamp in Unix epoch seconds; fractional seconds are allowed. JSON numbers parse as IEEE-754 doubles (roughly 15-17 significant digits), so true nanosecond precision does not survive most parsers; if that precision is genuinely needed, send integer nanoseconds since epoch.

path_indicator.description: This indicates if the point is used to start a path segment, or end a path segment. Point type surveys should include both a START and an END with the same coordinate.  For middle points, this is not used.

survey_path.description: A series of path_points with a reference to a data uri. For example, the surveyed data is included in a timestamped PCAP file. You can have multiple survey_path objects pointed at a single PCAP.

name.description: Optional name used to reference this survey path.

path_data_uri.description: URI reference to path data (absolute or relative). Not all URIs will be resolvable by all systems.

survey_device_sw_version.description: Software version of the survey device.

survey_device_identifier.description: Unique identifier of the survey device

host_device_platform.description: platform of the host device. For example, if using a survey tool like a WLAN-PI, this field would describe the controlling device (e.g., "iPhone Pro Max 16").

path_type.description: To keep logic simple for implementers, we should specify if the points in this path are Point (stop and go) or a Continuous (line) type survey.

path_points.description: Each path in the path points must have a START and END point. There can be multiple paths within the path_points, but each must contain a START and END point.  These points are ordered from start to end.

offset_value.description: A distance value with unit, used for translation/offset operations.

value.description: The offset distance value (can be positive or negative)

floor_transform.description: 2D transformation parameters for positioning and orienting a floorplan within a building coordinate system. Transformations are applied in order: scale, then rotation, then translation (offset).

scale_x.description: Horizontal scale factor to apply to the floorplan. A value of 1.0 means no scaling. Values greater than 1.0 enlarge, values less than 1.0 shrink. Must be a positive number.

scale_y.description: Vertical scale factor to apply to the floorplan. A value of 1.0 means no scaling. Values greater than 1.0 enlarge, values less than 1.0 shrink. Must be a positive number.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees to apply to the floorplan around its origin (lower-left corner). Positive values rotate counter-clockwise. This is applied after scaling and before translation.

x_offset.description: Horizontal (X-axis) offset to shift the floorplan. Applied after scaling and rotation. Positive values shift right.

y_offset.description: Vertical (Y-axis) offset to shift the floorplan. Applied after scaling and rotation. Positive values shift up.

building_floor.description: A floor within a building that references a floorplan and provides transformation parameters for positioning the floorplan within the building coordinate system.

floorplan_name.description: Reference to the name of a floorplan defined in the floorplans array. The floorplan must exist and its name must be unique.

floor_level.description: Integer representing the vertical position of this floor within the building. Higher values represent floors higher in the building. Floors are stacked top to bottom based on this value. Example: Ground floor = 0, First floor = 1, Basement = -1

floor_label.description: Human-readable label for the floor (e.g., "Ground", "Mezzanine", "Basement", "Roof"). Used for display purposes.

transform.description: 2D transformation parameters for positioning and orienting this floorplan within the building coordinate system.

building_address.description: Physical address information for a building. Uses international-friendly field names to support addresses worldwide.

address_lines.description: Flexible array of address lines (e.g., street address, suite number, building name). Supports any international address format.

locality.description: City, town, village, or equivalent locality name.

administrative_area.description: State, province, region, prefecture, or equivalent administrative division.

postal_code.description: Postal code, ZIP code, or equivalent.

country.description: Country name or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g., "US", "JP", "DE"). ISO alpha-2 codes are recommended for interoperability.

building.description: Representation of a building that groups multiple floorplans together with vertical ordering and transformation capabilities.

name.description: Unique name of the building (must be unique in the openintent payload). This name is referenced by floorplan.building_name, accesspoint.building_name, and switch.building_name properties.

address.description: Physical address information for the building.

coordinates.description: Location of the building, typically the centroid. Each entry may express the same position in a different unit or coordinate system; entries must describe the same point.

floors.description: Array of floor references with transformation properties. Floors are ordered top to bottom (highest floor_level is at the top of the building). This array is authoritative for grouping and stacking floorplans; floorplan.building_name is a denormalized back-reference and must agree with it.
